$comment: US-660: shared cases for resolveItem. Asserted by BOTH src/lib/kitchenLoopFixtures.test.ts and the Swift mirror (US-682). One shared context is declared here so both platforms resolve against identical tables.

$format.context: the household tables the resolver may look at: items (subset of foods), aliases (item_aliases), canonicalProducts (the shared seed). alias normalized_text values are ALREADY normalised, exactly as the column stores them.
$format.cases: each has name, input { text, barcode? }, and expected
$format.expected.itemId: when a concrete item is resolved
$format.expected.matchedBy: which rule won: barcode | alias_exact | alias_fuzzy | canonical_product | none
$format.expected.provisional: true when no household item was resolved; steps 4 and 5 both land here because canonical_products has no foods row in this household
$format.expected.proposedName: asserted only when present; the parent's own words, never the sorted normalised form
$format.expected.seed: asserted key by key when present; absent keys are not checked
$format.$note: Swift mirror: decode this whole file, build the context once, and assert each case. Do not reorder `aliases` — the fuzzy step picks the best score, and a stable order keeps ties deterministic across platforms.

LIMITATION: a transposition in a short string falls below threshold and is NOT absorbed
cases.$why: Classic Levenshtein scores a transposition as two edits, and similarity is normalised over string length, so 'mikl whole' vs 'milk whole' is 0.800 against a 0.82 threshold while the longer 'braest chicken' vs 'breast chicken' is 0.857 and passes. Whether a typo is forgiven therefore depends on how long the item name is, which is not a property anyone would choose. Damerau-Levenshtein would score this 0.900. Tracked as US-692; this case pins today's behaviour so the fix is visible when it lands.
